notes: EBIT is computed as GAAP Operating income = Gross profit − Total operating expenses from the consolidated statement of income (includes depreciation/amortization and restructuring/other operating costs in operating expenses). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040987/000004098726000003/gpc-20251231.htm))

Capex uses the 10-K 'Total capital expenditures' line; D&A uses the 10-K 'Depreciation and amortization' line from operating expenses. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040987/000004098726000003/gpc-20251231.htm))

Net working capital is computed using a balance-sheet convention: (Current assets − Cash) − (Current liabilities − Short-term borrowings − Current portion of debt). This is a model-convention and may differ from other NWC definitions (e.g., excluding dividends payable or treating lease-related current items differently). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040987/000004098726000003/gpc-20251231.htm))

NOL gross carryforwards are disclosed as approximately $504 million; NOL utilization percent (0.80) is an assumption because the filing does not provide a deterministic annual utilization schedule. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000040987/000004098726000003/gpc-20251231.htm))

Investments is set to null because a distinct, DCF-relevant 'investments' line item (separate from capex/acquisitions and balance-sheet 'other assets') was not extracted into a single standardized number for this pipeline. Override if your DCF implementation defines investments differently.
Base-case WACC (0.085) and terminal growth (2.0%) are modeling assumptions (not explicitly disclosed by management).
Current price (96.38) reflects the market-data snapshot timestamp from the finance tool (latest trade reported on 2026-03-20 UTC, which is closest to the requested research as-of date).

Peer multiples are sourced from StockAnalysis.com and treated as EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA proxies for EV/NTM; this is an approximation and may not match other vendors' NTM methodology. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/lkq/financials/ratios/))

Forecast drivers for 2027–2030 are not explicitly guided by management; they are set to be consistent with FY2026 guidance ranges and a normalized margin/return-on-investment recovery from the 2024–2025 cost-investment period. ([genpt.com](https://www.genpt.com/2026-02-17-Genuine-Parts-Company-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Results))

catalysts: Progress toward completing the announced separation into Global Automotive and Global Industrial businesses.
Ongoing restructuring and technology/supply-chain initiatives delivering cost savings and operating leverage.
Any improvement in Europe/industrial end-market demand that lifts comparable growth and margins.
company_overview: Genuine Parts Company is a global service provider of automotive and industrial replacement parts with a network of 10,800+ locations across North America, Europe, and Australasia.
FY2025 net sales were $24.3B, with automotive representing the majority of revenue and industrial providing diversified aftermarket exposure.
Business model emphasizes parts distribution scale, value-added solutions, and technology-enabled supply chain execution.
current_context: In its Feb 17, 2026 release for FY2025, management reported $24.3B sales (+3.5% YoY) and established FY2026 guidance for total sales growth of 3% to 5.5%.
FY2026 effective tax rate guidance is approximately 24%, with FY2026 free cash flow guidance of $550M to $700M.
Management also announced its intention to separate the Automotive Parts Group and the Industrial Parts Group into two independent publicly traded companies.
investment_highlights: Base case anchors revenue growth in management’s FY2026 sales-growth range and then transitions to a steady mid-single-digit profile consistent with aftermarket durability.
EBIT margin is modeled to normalize upward from 2024–2025 cost pressures toward a ~6.0% steady-state target as investment and restructuring effects fade.
Depreciation/amortization and capex intensities are held near recent levels to reflect ongoing technology and supply-chain enhancements without aggressive reinvestment assumptions.
Net working capital intensity stabilizes (rather than steadily expanding) to support sustained conversion of earnings into cash flow.
key_risks: Macro demand softness and pricing/volume volatility (especially in Europe) could keep margins below the modeled path.
Working-capital swings (inventory and payables timing) could reduce free cash flow conversion versus expectations.
Higher interest rates, credit conditions, or unanticipated tax/pension-related items could raise effective discount rates and/or reduce cash generation.
